summary: Petition under Section 79 (1) (b) and (f) of the Electricity Act, 2003, for adjudication of disputes pertaining to the Scheduled Delivery Date and illegal recovery of Liquidated Damages by the TNPDCL from the KSKMPCL under the PPA dated 27.11.2013. - _(c) Pass such other further order(s) as the Hon’ble Commission may deem just in the facts of the present case._ _Order in Petition No.349/MP/2024 Page_ **_3_** _of_ **_17_** _Order in Petition No.349/MP/2024 Page_ **_5_** _of_ **_17_** decision of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in C.A. No. 10480/2024 is misplaced, as the dispute is a tariff dispute and falls exclusively within the jurisdiction of the Commission, in terms of Section 79(1)(f) and (b) of the Act regarding regulation of tariffs. - h) Claiming LD is reagitating the settled issues which have been settled by the Hon’ble Supreme Court, and attempting to impose liability for a hypothetical non-event, and therefore, liable to be rejected. There can be no surviving claim for the period from 1.6.2014 to 1.10.2015 in terms of the Commission’s order 11. The matter was heard on 12.11.2024, wherein the learned counsel for the KSKMPCL and the learned counsel for TNPDCL made detailed oral submissions. The Commission, after seeking certain additional information from KSKMPCL, permitted the parties to file their written submissions on the question as to whether the dispute is a non-tariff dispute referrable to arbitration, in terms of the APTEL's judgment dated 28.8.2024 in Appeal No. 309/2024. Subject to this, the order in the petition was reserved. _Order in Petition No.349/MP/2024 Page_ **_8_** _of_ **_17_** - e) The present Petition does not fall within the adjudicatory jurisdiction of this Commission and is to be referred to the arbitration, as the subject matter falls under the category of non-tariff related disputes, that may be referred to arbitration in terms of Article 14.3.2.1 of the PPA. APTEL in its judgment dated 14.11.2022 in Appeal No. 397/2022 _(APSPDCL v APERC & ors)_ held that the jurisdiction of Electricity Regulatory Commissions only extends to tariff related disputes and that the referral of non-tariff related disputes to arbitration is mandatory, as otherwise, the arbitration clause is rendered redundant. The APTEL has also specifically held that simpliciter money claims such as Late - a) The alleged claim of delay and LD is contrary to the PPA and orders from the Commission and APTEL. The claim for the period from 1.6.2014 to 25.8.2014 due to a _force majeure_ event of transmission corridor non-availability, falling within the SDD, had been settled by this Commission, affirmed by APTEL and the Hon’ble Supreme Court. The claim for the alleged delay in the commissioning and LD squarely falls within the jurisdiction of this Commission. The decision of APTEL in Appeal No. 309/2019 specifically categorizes the above dispute, being a dispute arising out of a force majeure event, delay in commissioning, etc., as a dispute within the jurisdiction of the Commission. **_“Whether the relief sought for by KSKMPCL in the present petition is a tariff dispute to be adjudicated by the Commission or a non-tariff dispute referable to arbitration, in terms of Section 79(1)(f) of the Act?”_** _(f) to adjudicate upon disputes involving generating companies or transmission licensee in regard to matters connected with clauses (a) to (d) above and to refer any dispute for arbitration;_ _14.3.1.1 a) where any Dispute arises from a claim made by any Party for any change in or determination of the Tariff or any matter related to Tariff or claims made by any Party which partly or wholly relate to any change in the Tariff or determination of any such claims could result in change in the Tariff shall be submitted to adjudication by the Appropriate Commission. Appeal against the decisions of the Appropriate Commission shall be made only as per the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003, as amended from time to time._ _b) Where SERC is appropriate commission, all disputes between the procurer and the seller shall be referred to SERC._ _2.3.2.1 If the Dispute arises out of or in connection with any claims not covered in Article 14.3.1.1 a) such Dispute shall be resolve by arbitration under the Indian Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 and the Rules of the Indian Council of Arbitration, in accordance with the process specified in this Article. In the event of such Dispute remaining unresolved as referred to in Article 14.2.1.3 hereof, any party to such Dispute may refer the matter to Registrar under the Rules of the Indian Counsel of Arbitration . “_ _Order in Petition No.349/MP/2024 Page_ **_14_** _of_ **_17_** 79(1)(f) and Section 158 of the Act, directs that the present dispute between the parties, shall be referred for arbitration. The Commission further directs that both the parties herein, shall within 30 (thirty) days from the date of this order, submit to the Commission, along with an affidavit, their list of two persons, each having relevant knowledge and expertise, for the Commission to choose one (out of the two persons) for appointment as Arbitrator(s) in the present case. While doing so, the parties shall keep in view the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation (Amendment) Act 2015, on the issue of independence/impartiality of the proposed Arbitrator(s). The third Arbitrator shall be nominated by the two Arbitrators appointed by the Commission.
